in_scope_scenarios: Users try to retrieve specific photos using vague cues (subject, person, date, location, event) via the app’s search bar, AI search, facial‑recognition name search, or manual scrolling. [IDs: 4,7,8,12,18,25,29,30,33,39,45,62,66,101,112,118,122,137,142,148,151,155]
remembered_landscape: Users often recall high‑level context such as the subject ('Dog in a hat'), a person’s face or name, approximate age (e.g., 6‑year‑old photos), download time, month boundaries, or that a screenshot was a favorite reference. [IDs: 12,18,25,29,30,33,39,45,62,137,142,148,151,122]
forgotten_landscape: Exact file names, album titles, precise timestamps, folder locations, and detailed content of screenshots are frequently forgotten. [IDs: 33,151,137]
search_behaviors: Typical behaviors include entering keyword queries, using AI‑powered search, searching by person name, scrolling through years or ‘Recently Added’, manually browsing thousands of screenshots, and downgrading the app after UI changes. [IDs: 4,7,8,25,29,30,33,62,101,112,118,122,137,146,148,52]
retrieval_failures: The dominant failure mode is QUERY → RETRIEVAL FAILURE (e.g., ids 4,7,8,12,18,29,30,33,39,42,45,52,54,59,62,66,101,112,118,122,146,148,149,155). One case of RETRIEVAL → RECOGNITION FAILURE occurs with facial‑recognition name search (id 25). SEARCH RECOVERY FAILURE appears when UI changes prevent easy scrolling (ids 62,146).
opportunities:
- AI‑enhanced query refinement to map vague language to visual concepts.
- Semantic indexing that links subjects, people, dates, and locations regardless of exact wording.
- Persistent, searchable metadata (album titles, timestamps, download IDs) that survives UI updates.
- Improved facial‑recognition tagging and user‑editable name associations.
- UI designs that retain clear date/month separators and allow quick jump to time ranges.
- Backup‑visibility cues that surface backed‑up items in search results.
- Faster “Recently Added” shortcuts for screenshots and other high‑frequency media.
